§7 POST-ER ACTION PLAYBOOK · if-then rules pre-committed
mechanical reaction template · what triggers what · no improvisation at the open
4 scenarios · pre-committed
A · BEAT & GAP UP
IF EPS surprise ≥ +4% AND gap ≥ +3% AND rev-surp ≥ +1% at open
→ PEAD handoff · enter day-after on 1H reclaim of opening range high · stop = gap-fill 50% · target +5d +4.6% median · size 0.5R initial · scale 0.25R on continuation
B · MISS & GAP DOWN
IF EPS surprise < 0% OR gap ≤ −4% AND volume > 2.5× avg
→ STAND DOWN 48h · do not catch · let day-2 dip-buyers establish floor · if Mode A position was open, sleeve exits day-before so N/A here · only re-enter after ER+5d on EMA21 reclaim
C · IN-LINE & NO MOVE
IF |EPS surprise| < 2% AND |1-day gap| < 2%
→ VOL-CRUSH HARVEST · short straddle / iron condor on ER+1 open if IVR remains above pre-ER 30d avg minus 15pp · size 0.5R · close on 50% premium captured (typically 2–3d)
D · BEAT BUT FADE
IF EPS surprise ≥ +4% AND gap-up open BUT close < pre-ER VWAP by EOD
→ BEAR FLAG ALERT · this is the Q3'25 pattern · sell-the-news + guide-down distribution · re-enter only on EMA50 reclaim with vol · do NOT defend pre-ER thesis
Pre-commitment principle: every action above is decided before the print. The 09:30 ET open is a high-emotion / low-information environment — the worst time to decide. Rules ship to alerts; alerts fire mechanically.

Vol-crush expectation: IVR ramps from 32% → ~52% over the next 21 days, then crashes ~30pp on the ER open. That's the structural payoff of Mode A exit-day-before — you've already captured the pre-drift; you don't pay the −30pp crush. For Mode C holders or fresh post-ER entrants, the crush is the cost of admission to the directional move.
